summary: Walkthrough for putting a strand groom on an animated skeletal mesh: enable skin cache and groom plugins, import an Alembic groom, add a Groom component to SKM_Manny, create a Groom Binding asset, build a Hair shading-model material, and enable hair physics simulation.
gotchas: Plugins and Support Compute Skin Cache need an editor restart
Hair material must use Shading Model Hair and Use with Hair Strands
Binding asset is optional but avoids GPU projection cost at startup

summary: Explains the groom import flow (DCC to Alembic .abc to Groom asset, optional binding, Groom component) and documents every field in the Groom Import Options dialog: conversion rotation/scale, per-group decimation, guide types and interpolation settings.
gotchas: Requires Alembic Groom Importer and Groom plugins plus restart
High/Medium interpolation quality can take several dozen minutes to build
Rigged Guides intended only for low guide counts (ponytails, dreadlocks)

summary: Shows how to build a Deformer Graph that deforms a groom on the GPU: Primary node set to Groom Component, Groom/Guides inputs, a Custom Compute Kernel with HLSL in the Shader Text Editor, and a Write Groom output, then assign it via Mesh Deformers on the Groom component; includes a wave-offset kernel example.
gotchas: Requires Deformer Graph plugin and restart
Write Groom can only write attributes that already exist on the groom
Time/game-dependent effects only visible when Playing or Simulating
Kernel dispatches in groups (default 64), so guard Index against control point count

summary: Lists the project setting and plugins needed to import and render grooms: Support Compute Skin Cache for morph/deformer-driven skinning, plus Alembic Groom Importer, Groom, optional Hair Card Generator and Deformer Graph, with default enabled states.
gotchas: Built-in groom skinning supports bone-based deformation only; morph targets/deformers need Skin Cache
Setting and plugins require an editor restart
Alembic Groom Importer and Groom are disabled by default

summary: Covers Groom Binding assets that skin a groom to a Skeletal Mesh or Geometry Cache: creating one via Create Binding, source/target meshes, RBF interpolation points, attaching via Groom component, per-LOD Rigid vs Skinning binding type, and viewport visualization of root bindings.
gotchas: No binding needed for rigid attachment
Binding data only used when the LOD Binding Type is Skinning
Geometry Cache binding requires the Geometry Cache plugin
Source and Target meshes must share UV mapping

summary: Reference for the Groom Asset Editor Cards and Meshes panels: assigning card/mesh geometry and textures (depth, coverage, tangent, attributes) per hair group and LOD, card guide types, texture layouts, and the Hair Card Generator plugin for converting strands to cards.
gotchas: Hair Card Generator is experimental; results vary with groom complexity
Generated guide type assumes card geometry made of triangle bands

summary: Explains groom LODs in the Groom Asset Editor LOD panel: LOD Mode (Default/Auto/Manual), Auto LOD Bias, up to 8 LODs per hair group using Strands, Cards or Meshes geometry, per-LOD decimation, screen size, binding type, simulation and RBF overrides, and LOD preview stats.
gotchas: Up to 8 LOD entries per hair group
Meshes geometry type supports only RBF (no skinning or simulation)
Decimation and screen size only editable when LOD Mode is Manual

summary: Specification of the Alembic schema Unreal expects for groom files: ICurves geometry, width handling, groom_ attribute naming, Constant/Uniform/Vertex scopes, and the table of general and geometry attributes such as groom_guide, groom_group_id, groom_root_uv and groom_color.
gotchas: Property names must be lowercase with groom_ prefix
Width falls back to 1 cm if no groom_width or convertible width
kUniformScope width is supported but untested
Unreal provides no grooming tool; groom in an external DCC

summary: Describes Groom Caches (Alembic grooms with time samples) for playing back DCC-simulated hair: Guides vs Strands cache types, the Groom Cache import options, assigning a cache to a Groom component, and driving it with a Groom Cache track in a Level Sequence.
gotchas: Cache and Groom Asset must have identical topology
Cannot assign a Groom Cache when a Groom Binding is already set
Guides caches need simulation enabled on every groom group to show in PIE
Strands cache must include vertex position animation

summary: Maya-side guide for preparing legacy XGen grooms for Unreal: converting guides to NURBS curves and descriptions to Interactive Grooms, exporting splines to Alembic, Maya Python scripts that add groom_group_id, groom_guide and groom_root_uv attributes, and the Export Selection to Alembic settings.
gotchas: Written against Maya 2018.6
Without guide curves, 10% of hairs become guides on import by default
Groom in the level must have width greater than 0

summary: How to use the Datasmith Attributes modifier in 3ds Max to control per-object export: choosing an existing lightmap UV channel, assigning a custom convex collision mesh, or exporting only bounding-box geometry.
gotchas: Custom collision mesh must be fully convex with matching pivot
Imported Light Map Coordinate Index may differ from the 3ds Max channel number due to re-indexing

summary: Reference for the Datasmith tab added to the 3ds Max ribbon: Direct Link sync and auto sync, .udatasmith export options including animated transforms, texture resolution and XRef settings, plus the Connection Status and Messages windows.
gotchas: Datasmith only exports visible objects
Export statistics for Direct Link sync are off unless enabled via MaxScript

summary: Explains each material Blend Mode (Opaque, Masked, Translucent, Additive, Modulate, AlphaComposite, AlphaHoldout) with visual examples, the Opacity Mask Clip Value for masked materials, and the final-color formula and lighting compatibility of each mode.
gotchas: Translucent and Additive do not support specularity and are not compatible with dynamic lighting
Opacity Mask Clip Value is not meant to be changed at runtime
Modulate does not support lighting or Separate Translucency
AlphaHoldout needs Unlit and only works against Translucent/Additive/Modulate/AlphaComposite surfaces

summary: Describes every material Shading Model (Unlit, Default Lit, Subsurface, Preintegrated Skin, Clear Coat, Subsurface Profile, Two Sided Foliage, Hair, Cloth, Eye, Single Layer Water, Thin Translucent, From Material Expression) with the material inputs each one exposes.
gotchas: Unlit emissive only lights the scene with Lumen or Lightmass Use Emissive for Static Lighting
Building a custom Eye material is not recommended; reuse the Digital Humans eye material

summary: Reference for vector math material nodes: AppendVector, ComponentMask, CrossProduct, DeriveNormalZ, DotProduct, Normalize, Transform (tangent/world/local/view space) and TransformPosition, with examples such as a camera-facing sphere-mapped texture.
gotchas: VertexColor and the Transform node are mutually exclusive (VertexColor comes out white)
Transform node does not handle non-uniform scaling correctly
No need to normalize values plugged into the Normal output
TransformPosition currently only supports transforming into world space

summary: Option-by-option reference for the Interchange Pipeline Configuration window when importing files: common offsets, mesh build options, static mesh collision and Nanite/lightmap build settings, skeletal mesh, animation, material and texture options, and which options remain for File > Import Into Level.
keys: Import Collision According to Mesh Name
gotchas: Import Lods requires Bake Meshes enabled in the pipeline
Import Only Animations requires a valid Skeleton
Bone Influence Limit above the Project Settings value has no effect
Import Into Level supports only FBX, glTF, GLB and MaterialX

summary: Overview of the Interchange import framework: pipelines, pipeline stacks and factories, the import/preview/conflict windows, importing at runtime via Blueprint (Interchange Manager), Python import, editing pipeline stacks in Project Settings, and creating custom pipelines in Blueprint, C++ or Python.
gotchas: FBX import through Interchange is Experimental and toggled by console commands
Runtime Blueprint import does not support Skeletal Mesh or Animation data
Cooked apps using Interchange at runtime must add the Interchange folder to Additional Asset Directories to Cook
Material assignment can no longer be preserved/replaced from the conflict window

summary: Hub page: introduces the Interchange Framework as a pipeline-based import framework and links to its development guides and file-format reference pages.

Steps to apply Eye-Dome Lighting to LiDAR point clouds through a Post Process Volume material (M_PP_EDL_MainPass for everything or M_PP_EDL_CustomPass for Custom Depth objects) to emphasize edges and depth.
gotchas: Combining with Ambient Occlusion may make the image too dark
CustomPass option increases cost because of Custom Depth

summary: Overview of the LiDAR Point Cloud plugin: supported formats (xyz/pts/txt, las/laz, e57), import/export scaling, global point budget, on-demand streaming, Lidar Clipping Volumes, and caveats for modifying point data at runtime.
gotchas: Up to 16 clipping volumes per level
Newly imported assets cannot stream until saved
Runtime-inserted points must stay within asset bounds or LOD breaks

summary: Quick start for the LiDAR Point Cloud plugin: enable LiDAR Point Cloud Support, import a cloud into a LidarPointCloudActor, build collision in Lidar Mode for PIE exploration, and select/hide/delete/crop points.
gotchas: Collision must be rebuilt after editing points
Plugin must be enabled and editor restarted

summary: Reference for LiDAR Point Cloud plugin project settings (octree, performance, collision, automation, import/export), actor Appearance and Rendering details, and r.Lidar* console variables controlling point budget and LOD importance.
gotchas: Use Fast Rendering quadruples VRAM usage and can crash at very high budgets
r.LidarTargetFPS is disabled when r.LidarPointBudget > 0
Gap Filling costs about 0.7 ms per million points

summary: Explains per-culture asset replacement via Content/L10N/<culture>/ folders, localizing fonts (composite fonts vs per-culture assets), Dialogue Wave and Dialogue Sheet based voice localization, and Asset Groups that give audio a separate culture.
gotchas: Localized assets are not hot-reloaded on runtime culture change; restart needed
Blueprints and other bytecode assets cannot be localized
Content Browser asset localization options require LocRes files for the cultures
Pick Dialogue Filename Format before recording audio

summary: Overview of Unreal localization and internationalization: ICU data sets, culture codes and fallback, Chinese/Spanish variants and culture mappings, Localization Targets, the gather/export/import/compile pipeline with manifest/archive/PO/LocRes files, PO formats, and packaging settings.
gotchas: LocRes is the only runtime source; changes must be compiled to take effect
Internationalization Support set must overlap the packaged localizations
Fake native culture workaround (es-US-POSIX) is unsupported; use String Tables

summary: Describes the Localization Dashboard for managing targets and running Gather/Export/Import/Compile, the Translation Editor and Translation Picker, and automating localization with the UAT Localize script and OneSky/XLOC providers.
gotchas: Localization Dashboard is classed experimental
New targets need a loading policy (typically Game) or they are not loaded at runtime
Translation Picker is experimental and must be enabled in Editor Preferences
Localize script is hard-coded for a Win64 Development Editor build

summary: How to query and set the active language, locale and asset-group cultures from C++/Blueprint via UKismetInternationalizationLibrary, override defaults in DefaultGame.ini or command line, preview languages in PIE/UMG, and configure culture remapping and restrictions.
gotchas: Console culture commands only work in non-shipping builds
PIE/UMG previews only load localization data and are not fully accurate; use standalone (-game) for that

summary: Tips for speeding up localization text gathering using asset gather caches, why bytecode assets cannot be cached, and GatherText commandlet arguments to report or fix stale/missing caches.
gotchas: Blueprints and levels with non-empty Level Blueprints cannot generate gather caches
Cache fix options are not in the Localization Dashboard; run the commandlet manually

summary: Detailed guide to FText: LOCTEXT/NSLOCTEXT literals, FText::Format and the Format Text node with plural/gender/Hangul argument modifiers, culture-aware number/date/case generation in C++ and Blueprint, text marshalling formats, stable Data Table keys, polyglot data and localized text sources.
gotchas: Converting FText to FString loses text history and localization data
Importing raw strings generates new unstable keys each time
Time generation assumes UTC input unless given FText::GetInvariantTimeZone()

summary: How to create String Tables in C++ (LOCTABLE macros), from CSV, or as an asset, reference entries from C++, INI or FText properties, and redirect renamed tables or keys.
gotchas: CSV string tables are not staged automatically; add their folder to Additional Non-Asset Directories to Package
String Table assets are binary and cannot merge conflicts
String Table editor cannot edit metadata
CSV needs Key and SourceString columns; quotes escaped as double quotes

summary: Covers importing MaterialX (.mtlx) directly or via USD, the Volumetric Material and Normals from Height options, Project Settings > Interchange MaterialX function mappings for Substrate and non-Substrate projects, and how transmission/subsurface and OpenPBR materials are converted.
gotchas: Displacement only visible on Nanite-enabled meshes, and Nanite does not support transparent materials
Transmission and subsurface cannot be evaluated in the same shading path
Do not edit engine material functions; copy them into the project
Full OpenPBR fidelity needs Substrate Adaptive GBuffer, which adds cost

summary: Lists Unreal's MaterialX extensions: the ND_ue_displacement_float node, the AD_ue_displacement_attribute custom attribute, and sparse_volume support for Sparse Volume Textures, defined in Interchange_defs.mtlx.

Reference of which MaterialX version, shading models (Standard Surface, USD Preview Surface, OpenPBR, glTF) and node categories (PBR, NPR, CM, texture, procedural, math, geometric, compositing, etc.) Unreal supports, with per-node unsupported inputs and geompropvalue handling.

Disney Principled BSDF is not supported
OpenPBR and glTF Surface need Substrate; BSDF nodes are pass-through
Standalone .mtlx geompropvalues unsupported except vector2 'st'

summary: Tutorial building an Actor Action Utility Editor Utility Blueprint that simplifies selected static meshes to a target triangle count using Geometry Scripting (copy to dynamic mesh from a global pool, Apply Simplify to Triangle Count, copy back), with a pasteable Blueprint graph.
keys: Request and Release from Global Pool
gotchas: Geometry Scripting is Beta

Without Supported Classes the action shows for every actor class

keys: Create New Static Mesh Asset From Mesh
gotchas: Geometry Scripting is Beta
GeneratedDynamicMeshActor only appears with the Geometry Script plugin enabled
3D widgets only appear in Selection Mode

summary: Introduction to the Geometry Scripting plugin for generating and editing meshes from Blueprint and Python: UDynamicMesh, UDynamicMeshComponent, ADynamicMeshActor and AGeneratedDynamicMeshActor, the Target Mesh/Options node pattern, dynamic mesh pools, and component limitations versus static meshes.
gotchas: Beta feature

summary: Explains the Modeling Mode Mesh Element Selection toolbar for selecting triangles, edges, vertices and PolyGroups directly, transforming them with the gizmo, selection settings and hotkeys, and the Select category tools such as Extrude, Inset, Bevel, Insert Loops and Weld.

gotchas: Beta feature
